title: Intrinsic Motivation in Reinforcement Learning: A Research Agenda for Adaptive Self-Organisation
abstract: arXiv:2609.17325v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Biological cells can be viewed as individual, interacting agents whose collective dynamics give rise to adaptive behaviour at multiple levels of organisation, from individual cells through tissues to whole multicellular organisms. In this perspective and tutorial article we discuss whether intrinsic rewards in artificial neural systems can support adaptation, functional specialisation and higher-level self-organisation without a shared external objective. We review empowerment, curiosity, learning progress, information gain, unsupervised skill discovery, mutual information estimation and the use of world models for intrinsic reward computation. Particular attention is given to failure modes showing when such objectives do not produce sustained exploration or increasingly complex behaviour. We argue that more capable systems may require complementary objectives, communication, memory, learning at multiple temporal scales and environmental

translated_title: 强化学习中的内在动机：适应性自组织的研究议程
translated_abstract: 生物细胞可以被看作是个体的、相互作用的智能体，其集体动力学在多个组织层次上产生适应性行为，从单个细胞到组织再到整个多细胞生物体。在这篇观点与教程文章中，我们讨论了人工神经系统中的内在奖励能否在没有共享外部目标的情况下支持适应、功能专业化和更高层次的自组织。我们回顾了赋权、好奇心、学习进步、信息增益、无监督技能发现、互信息估计以及使用世界模型进行内在奖励计算等方法。我们特别关注了这些目标的失败模式，即它们何时无法产生持续的探索或日益复杂的行为。我们认为，更强大的系统可能需要互补的目标、通信、记忆、多时间尺度的学习以及环境因素。
tldr: 本文探讨了强化学习中内在奖励机制能否在缺乏外部目标的情况下支持适应、功能专业化和更高层次的自组织，系统回顾了赋权、好奇心、信息增益等内在动机方法及其失败模式，并提出了结合互补目标、通信与多时间尺度学习的未来研究议程。
en_tdlr: This paper examines whether intrinsic rewards in reinforcement learning can support adaptation, functional specialisation, and higher-level self-organisation without external objectives, systematically reviewing methods such as empowerment, curiosity, and information gain, analyzing their failure modes, and proposing a research agenda incorporating complementary objectives, communication, and multi-timescale learning.
